title: kate-core: test a line inside a fold span
summary: span_contains_line is true when the line is after the start and before the end. The header line and the end line are outside. The test goes in the existing fold tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn span_contains_line(span: FoldSpan, line: u32) -> bool

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: fold.rs is a private module of view.rs. Its one test module is mod tests.  Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Add span_contains_line with the dead_code attribute above the pub fn. Return line > span.start && line < span.end. Do not touch indent_folds, innermost_fold, fold_at, fold_end, line_indents, or leading_indent. The test span_contains_line_is_open_at_both_ends uses FoldSpan { start: 0, end: 4 }. Line 0 returns false. Lines 1, 2, and 3 return true. Line 4 returns false. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: view::fold::tests::span_contains_line_is_open_at_both_ends
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because span_contains_line does not exist. A span of 0..4 contains lines 1, 2, and 3. It does not contain line 0 or line 4.
